newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE moves shares to Beirut bourse on Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE moves shares to Beirut bourse on Sept 30.

text.p: SOLIDERE, the $2-billion real estate company rebuilding war-damaged central Beirut, will move its shares to the official Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) as of September 30, the bourse officially announced on Saturday.

"Monday, September 30 has been set as the date for the start of trading in the company's shares," BSE chairman Gabriel Sehnaoui said in a statement. SOLIDERE shares have been trading on the privately-operated Beirut Secondary Market since mid-1994.

The SOLIDERE shares will add some $2 billion to the official bourse's capitalisation currently calculated at less than $400 million. The secondary market was set up in 1994 under central bank auspices.

Market sources have said that an important reason behind the move was a proposal to cross-list SOLIDERE shares on the Kuwait Stock Exchange, which had set a condition that it would only list shares that were traded on Lebanon's official bourse.
A shares are distributed to former holders of property rights in the central Beirut disctrict SOLIDERE is rebuilding and B shares were issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994.

The move will raise to nine the number of shares -- in five companies -- traded on the official exchange which has been lacklustre since it reopened in January after a 13-year closure during the 1975-90 civil war.
